overview: You are not one listener but about seven, and they take turns. The loudest is a pop-punk and Midwest-emo kid who never left the basement show (28% of your weighted listening, 32% of the recent stuff). Next comes a songwriter-first modern pop era led by Olivia Rodrigo (19%), then a classic-rock, roots and heartland streak that reads like a Milwaukee summer radio dial (16%), and an Americana and alt-country fan who likes songwriters with dirt on their boots (14%, though that one has gone quiet since Dec 2025). Behind them sit a musical-theatre habit that gets binged in bursts (Operation Mincemeat owned your October 2026), an indie and alternative rock layer that connects the others, and a jam-band and bluegrass streak. Hip-hop and EDM are occasional side quests, not a profile. The profiles rarely overlap in genre, but they share a through-line: hooks, real instruments, and singers who sound like they mean it. Two thirds of the artists in your data have under 100k Deezer fans, so you dig deeper than most listeners.
closing: What ties it together: you reward songwriting over production, you binge an album or cast recording hard and then move on (Olivia Rodrigo's 'you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love' got 200 plays, Operation Mincemeat took over a whole month), and you keep circling back to the same handful of lifers (Beach Bunny, Green Day, Weezer, The Front Bottoms, CCR, Rise Against, Gracie Abrams). Your centre of gravity is American (about 80% of your artists) and born in the 1990s, with the classic-rock profile as the one real excursion into the 60s and 70s. The recommendations lean into all of that: each playlist starts from songs you already love and reaches outward one step at a time, household names are kept to one side, and the Americana lane gets extra attention because it is the one that has drifted.

P1.desc: This is the core of your listening and the most consistent across every time window. It runs from the big pop-punk canon (Green Day, blink-182, The Offspring, Sum 41, Good Charlotte, Fall Out Boy, Taking Back Sunday) into the sadder, wordier Midwest-emo and emo-revival wing (The Front Bottoms, Modern Baseball, Joyce Manor, Mom Jeans., Remo Drive, Sorority Noise, Hot Mulligan, Spraynard) and the newer fuzzy pop side (Beach Bunny, STELLA LEFTY, The Linda Lindas). 'Twin Size Mattress', 'Your Graduation', 'Sports' and 'Coming Clean' are the signature songs. What you like here is shouted, slightly off-key sincerity: confessional lyrics, fast drums, singalong choruses, and bands small enough to still play 300-cap rooms. Rise Against and The Menzingers add the political and punk-rock edge. Beach Bunny is the single most consistent artist in your entire dataset (in all 10 lists, number 1 in Dec 2025), and Green Day, The Front Bottoms, Modern Baseball, blink-182 and Taking Back Sunday are all loyal across both snapshots. This profile is also where the recommendation engine is most confident: the emo-revival canon you have not touched yet (Tigers Jaw, The Hotelier, Brand New, American Football, Jeff Rosenstock, PUP, The Wonder Years, Free Throw) is pointed at by almost every band you love here.
P1.playlist_blurb: Midwest emo, pop punk and fuzzy indie punk. Starts from The Front Bottoms and Modern Baseball and reaches out to the bands that share their bills.

P2.desc: Your second pillar is roots music with a songwriter at the centre: alt-country and Americana (Waxahatchee, Justin Townes Earle, John Prine, Steve Earle, Turnpike Troubadours, The Red Clay Strays), the new wave of storytelling country-folk (Stephen Wilson Jr., Cameron Whitcomb, Noah Kahan, Jesse Welles, Wednesday, MJ Lenderman) and the folk-punk and Celtic strand (The Pogues, The Dubliners, The Walker Roaders, The Mountain Goats, John Craigie). The older end reaches Jim Croce, Joan Baez, Bob Dylan, Johnny Cash and Cat Stevens. 'Bad Apple', 'Gary', 'Crowbar', 'Cherry Hard Candy' and 'Elderberry Wine' are the tells. You like voices with grain, acoustic guitars that still hit hard, and lyrics that tell a specific story about a specific place. This was your big late-2025 lane (Waxahatchee, Justin Townes Earle, Wednesday and The Red Clay Strays were all top 30 in the Dec 2025 snapshot) and it has gone quiet in 2026: only 7% of recent weight versus 14% overall. It is also your most under-the-radar profile, with 81% of its artists under 100k Deezer fans. The recommendations here are built to bring it back.
P2.playlist_blurb: Alt-country, Americana, folk punk and the new storytelling country-folk. Waxahatchee and John Prine as the compass.

P3.desc: A smaller but very distinct lane: Grateful Dead and Billy Strings at the top (both rising in 2026, Billy Strings was your number 2 artist over the last six months), Allman Brothers Band as the Southern-rock backbone, the college-jam lineage of DISPATCH, Guster, O.A.R. and Trampled by Turtles, and the reggae-rock cousins Sublime, Dirty Heads and Rebelution. 'Whipping Post', 'Quinn the Eskimo (Live, 1985)' and 'I'm One of Those' carry it. This is your live-music taste: long songs, players who can actually play, and bands you would drive to a festival for. It is only 7% of your weight, but it is the profile most likely to turn into concert tickets, and the recommendations (Phish, Widespread Panic, Greensky Bluegrass, Hot Tuna, Jerry Garcia solo) are the natural next shows.
P3.playlist_blurb: Jam bands, newgrass and Southern roots rock. For long drives and longer sets. Grateful Dead and Billy Strings set the pace.

P4.desc: The roots-and-heartland side, and your third biggest profile at 16%: Creedence Clearwater Revival and The Band (both loyal, in every window, and both back in the Nov 2026 top 10 along with 'The Weight' and 'Have You Ever Seen The Rain'), John Mellencamp, Bob Seger, Steve Miller Band, Steely Dan, Fleetwood Mac, Jackson Browne, Warren Zevon, The Doors and The Rolling Stones, with a 90s alt-rock radio layer (Hootie & The Blowfish, Third Eye Blind, Collective Soul, Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters, Red Hot Chili Peppers) and a few swaggering modern rock bands (The Killers, Kings of Leon, Greta Van Fleet, The Struts). 'Roland the Headless Thompson Gunner', 'The Joker', 'Dani California' and 'My Hero' are the tells. It is the oldest profile by far (a third of these artists started before 1970) and the least obscure. It is less a discovery zone than a comfort zone: classic songs you have known your whole life, played when you want the radio to just be good. The biggest holes are obvious ones: Tom Petty, Neil Young, Lynyrd Skynyrd and the Eagles are absent from every list.
P4.playlist_blurb: Classic rock, roots rock, heartland songwriters and the 90s alt-rock radio dial. CCR, The Band, Mellencamp and Zevon, then one step sideways.

P5.desc: Your most-played single artist (Olivia Rodrigo, 247 Volt plays and 200 on one album) lives here, alongside Gracie Abrams, Chappell Roan, Sabrina Carpenter, Taylor Swift, Tate McRae, Audrey Hobert, Lizzy McAlpine, Alessi Rose, ROLE MODEL, sombr and Conan Gray. It is modern pop with a songwriter's spine: diaristic lyrics, guitar-forward production, and a lot of overlap with the emo profile's emotional register (Olivia Rodrigo even duets with Robert Smith). The K-pop Demon Hunters moment ('Golden') and the nostalgic Hilary Duff plays sit at the edges. This profile is almost entirely 2024-2026 and it is where your most binge-style listening happens: a new album drops and you play it 20 times. It is also your most mainstream profile (median 130k Deezer fans), so the recommendations deliberately skip the obvious megastars (Billie Eilish, Ariana Grande and Harry Styles are parked in the 'household names' list) in favour of the next tier: Joshua Bassett, Renee Rapp, Holly Humberstone, Rina Sawayama, Sasha Alex Sloan.
P5.playlist_blurb: Songwriter-first modern pop and bedroom pop. Olivia Rodrigo and Gracie Abrams as anchors, then the next wave.

P6.desc: Musical theatre is a real profile, not a fluke: Operation Mincemeat was your number one artist in the Nov 2026 4-week window with five songs in the top 10, Hamilton, Schmigadoon!, Be More Chill ('Michael in the Bathroom'), Heathers (Barrett Wilbert Weed), Wicked (Kristin Chenoweth, Idina Menzel) and Frozen (Kristen Bell) all show up, and Bo Burnham and Tenacious D add the comedy-song wing. You go for witty, fast, lyric-dense writing and ensemble numbers rather than ballads. It binges hard: one show takes over for a month and then disappears from the 4-week list entirely. By fan counts it is your most niche profile (median 1,300 Deezer fans, because cast members are credited individually), and the recommendations are performers rather than shows: Jonathan Groff, Jeremy Jordan, Aaron Tveit and Christian Borle are the voices that fans of your shows play next.
P6.playlist_blurb: Cast recordings and comedy songs. Operation Mincemeat and Hamilton as the anchors, then the shows their fans binge next.

P7.desc: The connective tissue between the other profiles: Weezer (a lifer, top 10 in every window), Cage The Elephant, Geese (your big 2026 discovery, with 'Au Pays du Cocaine' and 'Cobra' both top 5 for six months), Hippo Campus, Glass Animals, Tame Impala, MGMT, M83, Djo, Beck, Car Seat Headrest, Black Kids, and the sad-indie songwriters Phoebe Bridgers, boygenius, Julien Baker, Lucy Dacus, Blondshell and Samia. It is indie rock with melody first and a little weirdness welcome. At 8% it is the profile with the most room to grow: most of these artists appear in only one or two of your lists, so the recommendations here (Death Cab for Cutie, Silversun Pickups, Fontaines D.C., Black Country, New Road) are the most likely to open a new lane.
P7.playlist_blurb: Indie and alternative rock from Weezer to Geese to the sad-indie songwriters. Melody first, then a little strange.

P8.desc: Not a full profile, but worth naming: a thin hip-hop line (Kanye West, Juice WRLD, The Notorious B.I.G., Young Money) and a few EDM and dance moments (Marshmello, Disco Lines, Seeb). These are occasional moods rather than a lane you dig in, so the recommendations here are few and conservative.
P8.playlist_blurb: The hip-hop and dance moments that occasionally crash the party.
